newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas busy for this weekend, then quiet until.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas busy for this weekend, then quiet until.

text.p: The UK spot gas market was split on Friday with interest divided into two periods, dealers said.

There was huge interest for this weekend, with a large number of deals recorded, and then there was a jump to October 1997 and beyond, with several deals done running as far as the 1998 gas year. But there was scant interest between this weekend and the end of the year, with only a couple of trades seen in between.

A wide contango has opened between gas year 97 and gas year 98. Trade was recorded at 14.05 pence in gas year 97 and at 14.60 pence in gas year 98, and this was in fact a year-on-year spread at 0.55 pence a therm.
Players explained the contango by saying they saw the Interconnector, the pipeline connecting Bacton with Zeebrugge which is due to open in October 1998, as a bullish factor for prices.

And there are also forecasts of generally increasing demand going into the future, related to the possibility of more gas-fired power stations and a general perception that gas use is set to increase. This is tending to keep the market in contango over the long term.
In addition to the trades reported below, it was widely rumoured that Q1 98 was done at 17.90 pence a therm and Q3 98 at both 12.30 pence and 12.50 pence.

TransCo announced its weather forecast for Saturday on Friday evening. It expects a temperature of 5.9 celsius, against a seasonal normal temperature of 3.8 celsius. Forecast demand is 299 million cubic metres, or 71 percent of peak day demand, and the probability of interruption in all Local Distribution Zones is described as "low".
